1	# AGENTS.md — PP_Recruiting (Baylor Football Player Personnel)
2	
3	Handoff document for a coding agent (Codex, Claude Code, or any other) picking
4	up this project cold. Read this file first, then `LOG.md` for how the project
5	got here. `CLAUDE.md` covers the same ground for Claude sessions; where the two
6	disagree, this file's §3 file table is the current one.
7	
8	Owner: Eric Rash. Last updated: 2026-09-14.
9	
10	## Where this project lives
11	
12	Working folder, Windows:
13	`G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\02_SPORTS\Football\PP_Recruiting`
14	
15	This is Google Drive, not OneDrive. An earlier copy under
16	`OneDrive - Baylor University\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\...` no longer exists.
17	Older session logs and Codex rollouts still point at that OneDrive path; ignore
18	them and use the path above.
19	
20	Workbooks, deliverables and the `Send/` folder stay here on Drive. Project
21	documentation and scripts are version controlled in the companion repo
22	`DEV\PP_Recruiting` (Windows: `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\PP_Recruiting`,
23	Mac: `~/DEV/PP_Recruiting`), pushed to `erash11/PP_Recruiting`. Read that repo's
24	`docs/STATUS.md` before starting a session.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## 1. What this project is
29	
30	A unified grading system for Baylor Football player personnel that couples
31	**Telemetry (Teamworks) trait percentiles** with the internal **S.T.A.Q.S.**
32	grading scale, so incoming transfer-portal data gets filtered down to the
33	players who deserve a scout's time.
34	
35	Two inputs, one system:
36	
37	- The scout's **STAQS grade is the grade of record.**
38	- Telemetry percentiles are **threshold flags** that say who to review and which
39	  STAQS factors the data already supports.
40	
41	Nothing is averaged, weighted, or blended into a composite. That was an explicit
42	design decision, not an oversight (§5).
43	
44	Audience for the deliverables is recruiting and personnel staff, not analysts.
45	
46	---
47	
48	## 2. Standing rules (do not violate)
49	
50	1. **Read-only in Telemetry.** Never edit, save, or submit anything in
51	   app.telemetry.fm. Scraping the rendered UI for read purposes is fine.
52	2. **Always create new files. Never overwrite.** Deliverables are numbered; the
53	   next revision is `006. ...`. The master `000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` is
54	   never modified under any circumstances.
55	3. **Do not read Telemetry's auth token or import its internal service
56	   classes.** Both were tried and are blocked. Scrape the rendered table.
57	4. **STAQS is the grade of record.** Any data output is labeled a starting point
58	   for the scout, never a grade.
59	5. **Append to `LOG.md`** whenever a numbered file is created, a design decision
60	   is made or reversed, or a technique is proven or ruled out. Newest entries at
61	   the bottom, absolute dates.
62	
63	---
64	
65	## 3. Files in this folder
66	
67	| File | Role |
68	|---|---|
69	| `000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` | **Master, read-only.** GRD SCALE, OFFENSE/DEFENSE EVAL KEY, SZ-SPD matrices, NIL/XFER pay scales, per-position tabs (QB, RB, WR, SLOT, TE, OT, OG, NT, END, JACK, ILB, CB, SAF, STAR, SPD). Authority for tiers and size-speed standards. Uses custom fonts (NCAA Baylor Bears, Bahnschrift). |
70	| `001. ... UNIFIED GRADING.xlsx` | Template workbook, 7 sample WRs, shows the format. 2026-09-02. |
71	| `001. ... FRAMEWORK.docx` | Written framework/explainer. |
72	| `002. ... UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026 LOADED).xlsx` | Proof of concept, 3,000 live portal players. 2026-09-03. |
73	| `003. ... COACH EXPLAINER.docx` | 6-page walkthrough of 002 for coaches/staff. |
74	| `003. ... UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx` | 002 restyled to the Baylor aesthetic. |
75	| `004. ... COACH BRIEF.docx` | 1.5-page version of the explainer. |
76	| `004. ... TEASER (AGM).docx` | One-page teaser for the assistant GM. |
77	| `005. ... TEASER (AGM, BAYLOR STYLE).docx` | 004 restyled off the 003 workbook. Current version of the teaser. |
78	| `CLAUDE.md` / `LOG.md` / `AGENTS.md` | Project context, development log, this handoff. |
79	| `_to_delete/` | Temp render artifacts. Session cannot delete files; move junk here. |
80	
81	Build scripts (`build2.py`, `load.py`) lived in a session container and are
82	**not** in this folder. Their logic is documented on the workbook README tab, in
83	`LOG.md`, and in §5-6 below. **Rebuilding them as committed, versioned scripts
84	in this folder is the single highest-value thing a coding agent can do here.**
85	
86	---
87	
88	## 4. The S.T.A.Q.S. system
89	
90	Eight factors, each scored **1 / 3 / 9**, summing to **8-72**.
91	
92	Five critical factors (all positions): **S**ize, **T**oughness, **A**thletic
93	Flexibility, **Q**uickness, **S**peed. Plus **3 position-specific** factors. QB
94	has its own set of 8.
95	
96	Tiers (also loaded as the Player Grade dropdown in Telemetry Scout Reports >
97	Settings):
98	
99	| Grade | Score | Elite traits | Color |
100	|---|---|---|---|
101	| AA | 60-72 | 7-8 | green `00B050` |
102	| AL | 48-59 | 5-6 | yellow `FFC000` |
103	| QS | 40-47 | 3-4 | black `404040` |
104	| FRP | 30-39 | 1-2 | grey `D8D8D8` |
105	| LIM | 24-29 | 0-1 | pink `ED6363` |
106	| NGE | 8-23 (dropdown 0-23) | 0 | red `C00000` |
107	
108	---
109	
110	## 5. The bridge (Telemetry to STAQS) — the core algorithm
111	
112	Implement exactly this. Every constant lives on the workbook **SETTINGS** tab
113	and must stay editable there rather than hardcoded in formulas.
114	
115	```
116	elite trait      := Telemetry percentile >= 75
117	deficiency       := Telemetry percentile < 25
118	graded traits    := traits with a numeric percentile for that player
119	elite share      := elite traits / graded traits
120	```
121	
122	Elite share (not raw count) is used because positions carry different numbers of
123	Telemetry traits — OL has 2, LB has 8 — so a raw count would systematically
124	punish linemen.
125	
126	Share maps to a projected band using the GRD SCALE's own elite-trait cut lines:
127	
128	```
129	>= .875 (7/8) -> AA
130	>= .625 (5/8) -> AL
131	>= .375 (3/8) -> QS
132	>= .125 (1/8) -> FRP
133	   0          -> LIM, or NGE when deficiencies exceed elite traits by 2+
134	                 with no elite share
135	```
136	
137	Guards and flags:
138	
139	- **Minimum 2 graded traits** to project a band; otherwise the row is `THIN`.
140	- **REVIEW** fires at elite share >= .375 (the QS floor).
141	- **Speed alert**: Play Speed or Deep Speed >= 90 ("documented difference making
142	  SPEED" on the GRD SCALE).
143	- **Size-Speed alert**: poor size with elite speed — the GRD SCALE's "must be
144	  special and offer a role" exception.
145	- **LOW SAMPLE** below 150 snaps. Telemetry itself blanks most traits under
146	  roughly 100 snaps.
147	
148	**What data can and cannot grade.** Data directly supports 4 of the 5 critical
149	factors (Speed, Quickness, Athletic Flexibility, Size from HT/WT) and offers
150	proxies for Toughness. Position-specific factors get partial support (see the
151	CROSSWALK tab). FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, and medical are **never**
152	data-graded.
153	
154	---
155	
156	## 6. Workbook structure (001 / 002 / 003)
157	
158	Tabs, in order:
159	
160	- **README** — what it is, the bridge, how to use, scope, cell legend, sources.
161	- **SETTINGS** — thresholds, band cut lines, simplified size standards by
162	  position. *All tuning happens here.*
163	- **GRADE SCALE** — the six tiers.
164	- **METRIC GLOSSARY** — what each Telemetry metric measures.
165	- **CROSSWALK** — which Telemetry metric informs which STAQS factor, by position.
166	- **POSITION MAP** — Telemetry position codes -> Baylor eval tabs -> trait counts.
167	- **PORTAL INPUT** — the paste sheet, 67 columns in 002. Grouped as Player
168	  Traits (all positions) / QB Traits / Advanced Stats. Percentiles 0-100; blank
169	  or `-` where a position carries no metric. Column order need not match
170	  Telemetry but **headers must**. HT in inches (6'1" = 73).
171	- **REVIEW BOARD** — all formulas, do not hand-edit. One row per PORTAL INPUT
172	  row (3,154 in 002). Columns: traits graded, elite traits, deficiencies, elite
173	  share, projected band, REVIEW?, speed alert, size-speed alert, critical
174	  deficiency, data-suggested SIZE / TOUGH / ATHLETIC / QUICK / SPEED values,
175	  best and worst trait, plus roster metadata.
176	
177	**Cell legend:** yellow fill `FFF2CC` with blue text = user input. Black text =
178	formula.
179	
180	**House styling** (workbooks and companion docs both): Arial throughout unless
181	the Baylor-style variant is called for; titles Arial 12pt bold Baylor green
182	`154734`; subtitles and notes 9pt grey `595959`; table header rows white bold on
183	`154734`; tier fills per §4. The "Baylor style" variants (003 xlsx, 005 docx)
184	additionally use NCAA Baylor Bears / Baylor Bears Font display type and
185	Bahnschrift body, with a black masthead bar. Those fonts render only on a
186	machine that has them installed; Word substitutes elsewhere.
187	
188	---
189	
190	## 7. Telemetry platform notes
191	
192	Telemetry Sports (app.telemetry.fm, branded Teamworks) is the recruiting and
193	scouting platform. Login is the user's; an agent without a browser session
194	cannot reach it.
195	
196	- **Transfer Portal** > Player Traits / Advanced Stats / Boxscore. Traits and
197	  stats appear only after filtering to a position or position group.
198	- **Scout Reports > Settings** holds the Player Grade dropdown, already loaded
199	  with the six STAQS tiers. Scout reports carry a numeric Score (0-72) plus the
200	  grade.
201	- **Documentation** pages (Glossary, Player Traits, Advanced Stats) embed
202	  signed-URL PDFs from s3 docs.telemetry.fm. The PDFs, not the UI tooltips, are
203	  the reliable definition source.
204	- Traits and advanced stats are **0-100 percentiles vs the same position** (FBS,
205	  2019-present, in-game tracking). Exceptions: Top End Speed is raw mph; QB Risk
206	  Level is a text label; Tackle Breaking is documented but absent from the
207	  portal grid; QB decision-making surfaces as "Target Selection"; the DB
208	  coverage stat surfaces as "EPA/Target".
209	- High school prospects have **no** Telemetry data. Grade them on the STAQS eval
210	  keys as usual.
211	
212	### Scraping the portal (proven 2026-09-02, read-only)
213	
214	- The table is **virtualized** (~20 rows in the DOM) at 100 rows per page.
215	  Scroll the table's scroll container, then click "Next page" by aria-label.
216	  Row key = name + Previous + Entered. About 3 s per page.
217	- Filter panel: Position combobox (remove chip, type code, click option), "Enter
218	  snap count" input, date range via calendar. Each calendar month arrow moves
219	  **two** months; the end date cannot exceed Telemetry's own "today".
220	- **"Apply Filters" sometimes needs a second click.** Verify the "Filter (n)"
221	  count afterward.
222	- If the pager shows Next disabled on page 1, reload. The filter survives a
223	  reload but window state does not, so **export scraped data before reloading.**
224	- Move big payloads out of the browser as gzip+base64.
225	
226	---
227	
228	## 8. Current state
229	
230	Proof of concept (002 / 003 xlsx) covers **3,000 portal players** who entered on
231	or after 1/1/2026 with 100+ snaps and an FBS/FCS previous team:
232	
233	WR 453 · CB 431 · IDL 311 · EDGE 303 · SAF 290 · OB-LB 256 · RB 231 · OT 190 ·
234	QB 156 · TE 156 · OG 155 · C 68
235	
236	Results as of 2026-09-03: **608 REVIEW flags** (144 of them uncommitted),
237	**32 AA** and **133 AL** projections.
238	
239	Known data caution: Top End Speed (the raw mph field) has implausible scraped
240	values, e.g. 39 mph. Verify against Telemetry before quoting it. It feeds no
241	flag today.
242	
243	Teaching case used in the coach-facing docs: **Michael Gravely Jr.** (SAF, Ball
244	State) — 5 elite of 7 traits, so an AL projection, but Player Impact in the 1st
245	percentile. The traits-versus-production example.
246	
247	---
248	
249	## 9. Next steps for an agent picking this up
250	
251	Eric's stated next step: **once the approach is approved, automate the pull.**
252	Concretely, in priority order:
253	
254	1. **Reconstruct the build as versioned code in this folder.** `build2.py`
255	   (workbook construction) and `load.py` (data load) exist only in a dead
256	   session container. Rebuild them from §5-6 with openpyxl so the workbook is
257	   reproducible from a data file rather than by hand.
258	2. **Automate the scrape** per §7, with the gotchas encoded as retries and
259	   assertions (the second Apply Filters click, the Filter (n) verification, the
260	   page-1 reload, export-before-reload).
261	3. **Add a refresh path** that regenerates the REVIEW BOARD against a new pull
262	   without touching prior numbered files. New pull = new numbered workbook.
263	4. **Add validation**: flag implausible raw values (Top End Speed), report trait
264	   coverage by position, and diff a new pull against the prior one so staff see
265	   who is newly flagged.
266	
267	Things deliberately out of scope: a weighted composite score, any write
268	operation against Telemetry, and data-grading of FBI, wiring, keep-ability,
269	character, or medical.
270	
271	---
272	
273	## 10. Conventions for whatever you write
274	
275	- New deliverables are numbered; the next is `006.`. Never overwrite an existing
276	  numbered file, and never touch `000.`.
277	- Scripts go in this folder with plain names (`scrape_portal.py`,
278	  `build_workbook.py`), not numbered.
279	- Python with openpyxl for workbooks; the docs were built with docx-js.
280	- Deletion is not permitted from the agent session on this machine. Move
281	  unwanted files into `_to_delete/` and tell Eric.
282	- Append a dated entry to `LOG.md` for anything you build or decide.
283	
284	## Imported Claude Cowork project instructions

## 4. The S.T.A.Q.S. system

Eight factors, each scored **1 / 3 / 9**, summing to **8-72**.

Five critical factors (all positions): **S**ize, **T**oughness, **A**thletic
Flexibility, **Q**uickness, **S**peed. Plus **3 position-specific** factors. QB
has its own set of 8.

Tiers (also loaded as the Player Grade dropdown in Telemetry Scout Reports >
Settings):

| Grade | Score | Elite traits | Color |
|---|---|---|---|
| AA | 60-72 | 7-8 | green `00B050` |
| AL | 48-59 | 5-6 | yellow `FFC000` |
| QS | 40-47 | 3-4 | black `404040` |
| FRP | 30-39 | 1-2 | grey `D8D8D8` |
| LIM | 24-29 | 0-1 | pink `ED6363` |
| NGE | 8-23 (dropdown 0-23) | 0 | red `C00000` |

---

## 5. The bridge (Telemetry to STAQS) — the core algorithm

Implement exactly this. Every constant lives on the workbook **SETTINGS** tab
and must stay editable there rather than hardcoded in formulas.

```
elite trait      := Telemetry percentile >= 75
deficiency       := Telemetry percentile < 25
graded traits    := traits with a numeric percentile for that player
elite share      := elite traits / graded traits
```

Elite share (not raw count) is used because positions carry different numbers of
Telemetry traits — OL has 2, LB has 8 — so a raw count would systematically
punish linemen.

Share maps to a projected band using the GRD SCALE's own elite-trait cut lines:

```
>= .875 (7/8) -> AA
>= .625 (5/8) -> AL
>= .375 (3/8) -> QS
>= .125 (1/8) -> FRP
   0          -> LIM, or NGE when deficiencies exceed elite traits by 2+
                 with no elite share
```

Guards and flags:

- **Minimum 2 graded traits** to project a band; otherwise the row is `THIN`.
- **REVIEW** fires at elite share >= .375 (the QS floor).
- **Speed alert**: Play Speed or Deep Speed >= 90 ("documented difference making
  SPEED" on the GRD SCALE).
- **Size-Speed alert**: poor size with elite speed — the GRD SCALE's "must be
  special and offer a role" exception.
- **LOW SAMPLE** below 150 snaps. Telemetry itself blanks most traits under
  roughly 100 snaps.

**What data can and cannot grade.** Data directly supports 4 of the 5 critical
factors (Speed, Quickness, Athletic Flexibility, Size from HT/WT) and offers
proxies for Toughness. Position-specific factors get partial support (see the
CROSSWALK tab). FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, and medical are **never**
data-graded.

---

## 6. Workbook structure (001 / 002 / 003)

Tabs, in order:

- **README** — what it is, the bridge, how to use, scope, cell legend, sources.
- **SETTINGS** — thresholds, band cut lines, simplified size standards by
  position. *All tuning happens here.*
- **GRADE SCALE** — the six tiers.
- **METRIC GLOSSARY** — what each Telemetry metric measures.
- **CROSSWALK** — which Telemetry metric informs which STAQS factor, by position.
- **POSITION MAP** — Telemetry position codes -> Baylor eval tabs -> trait counts.
- **PORTAL INPUT** — the paste sheet, 67 columns in 002. Grouped as Player
  Traits (all positions) / QB Traits / Advanced Stats. Percentiles 0-100; blank
  or `-` where a position carries no metric. Column order need not match
  Telemetry but **headers must**. HT in inches (6'1" = 73).
- **REVIEW BOARD** — all formulas, do not hand-edit. One row per PORTAL INPUT
  row (3,154 in 002). Columns: traits graded, elite traits, deficiencies, elite
  share, projected band, REVIEW?, speed alert, size-speed alert, critical
  deficiency, data-suggested SIZE / TOUGH / ATHLETIC / QUICK / SPEED values,
  best and worst trait, plus roster metadata.

**Cell legend:** yellow fill `FFF2CC` with blue text = user input. Black text =
formula.

**House styling** (workbooks and companion docs both): Arial throughout unless
the Baylor-style variant is called for; titles Arial 12pt bold Baylor green
`154734`; subtitles and notes 9pt grey `595959`; table header rows white bold on
`154734`; tier fills per §4. The "Baylor style" variants (003 xlsx, 005 docx)
additionally use NCAA Baylor Bears / Baylor Bears Font display type and
Bahnschrift body, with a black masthead bar. Those fonts render only on a
machine that has them installed; Word substitutes elsewhere.

---

## 7. Telemetry platform notes

Telemetry Sports (app.telemetry.fm, branded Teamworks) is the recruiting and
scouting platform. Login is the user's; an agent without a browser session
cannot reach it.

- **Transfer Portal** > Player Traits / Advanced Stats / Boxscore. Traits and
  stats appear only after filtering to a position or position group.
- **Scout Reports > Settings** holds the Player Grade dropdown, already loaded
  with the six STAQS tiers. Scout reports carry a numeric Score (0-72) plus the
  grade.
- **Documentation** pages (Glossary, Player Traits, Advanced Stats) embed
  signed-URL PDFs from s3 docs.telemetry.fm. The PDFs, not the UI tooltips, are
  the reliable definition source.
- Traits and advanced stats are **0-100 percentiles vs the same position** (FBS,
  2019-present, in-game tracking). Exceptions: Top End Speed is raw mph; QB Risk
  Level is a text label; Tackle Breaking is documented but absent from the
  portal grid; QB decision-making surfaces as "Target Selection"; the DB
  coverage stat surfaces as "EPA/Target".
- High school prospects have **no** Telemetry data. Grade them on the STAQS eval
  keys as usual.

### Scraping the portal (proven 2026-09-02, read-only)

- The table is **virtualized** (~20 rows in the DOM) at 100 rows per page.
  Scroll the table's scroll container, then click "Next page" by aria-label.
  Row key = name + Previous + Entered. About 3 s per page.
- Filter panel: Position combobox (remove chip, type code, click option), "Enter
  snap count" input, date range via calendar. Each calendar month arrow moves
  **two** months; the end date cannot exceed Telemetry's own "today".
- **"Apply Filters" sometimes needs a second click.** Verify the "Filter (n)"
  count afterward.
- If the pager shows Next disabled on page 1, reload. The filter survives a
  reload but window state does not, so **export scraped data before reloading.**
- Move big payloads out of the browser as gzip+base64.

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state

- 2026-09-14: repo created to version control the documentation and scripts for
  a project whose files live on Google Drive. No system logic changed.
- Proof of concept is complete and sitting in
  `003. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx`
  on Drive. 3,000 portal players loaded (entries on or after 1/1/2026, 100+
  snaps, FBS/FCS previous team). Results: 608 REVIEW flags, 144 of those
  uncommitted, 32 AA projections, 133 AL projections.
- Deliverables 001 through 007 are finished and on Drive. 007 is the AGM tool
  summary in Baylor style. Next deliverable number is 008.

## Settings currently implemented

- Elite percentile 75, poor percentile 25
- Minimum snaps 150 (LOW SAMPLE warns below this, does not suppress)
- Speed alert: Play Speed or Deep Speed at 90th percentile or higher, fires
  independently of the elite-share gate
- Review trigger: elite-trait share at or above 0.375
- Minimum graded traits to project a band: 2, else THIN

## Next

1. Deliverable 008, the one-page position-by-position screening matrix. Gap 1
   from the workbook review. Never produced. See `docs/open-work.md`.
2. Reconstruct `build2.py` and `load.py`. They existed only in a session
   container and are gone, so the 002 and 003 workbooks cannot currently be
   rebuilt from code. The algorithm is written out as pseudocode in the Drive
   folder's `AGENTS.md`. See `scripts/README.md`.
3. Automate the portal pull, once the approach is approved.

## Open questions

- The 75th percentile and 0.375 share thresholds have not been validated against
  real recruiting usefulness. Eric's own note: test known prospects, including
  players the filter misses, and measure both worthwhile reviews generated and
  worthwhile players overlooked, by position.
- The Drive folder's `CLAUDE.md` has a stale file table. Its `AGENTS.md` §3 is
  the current list. Decide whether to fix or retire that file.

## Gotchas

- Telemetry's calendar arrows move two months at a time, and the end date cannot
  exceed Telemetry's own "today".
- "Apply Filters" sometimes needs a second click. Check the "Filter (n)" count.
- If the pager shows Next disabled on page 1, reload. Filters survive a reload,
  window state does not, so export scraped data before reloading.
- The portal table is virtualized, roughly 20 rows in the DOM at 100 rows per
  page. Scroll the container, then click Next page by aria-label.

# 2026-09-15 meeting: potential Review Board changes

Source: Fireflies meeting `01M2K5PNEVK662KYQ74TK2DKWD`, "Sep 15, 01:36 PM"
(untitled in Fireflies), 51 minutes.
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/view/01M2K5PNEVK662KYQ74TK2DKWD

## What kind of meeting this was

A working session, not a formal change review. Eric walked a player personnel
staff member through the 003 workbook's REVIEW BOARD. Fireflies did not name
speakers. Speaker 3 is Eric (he built the tool and sent the files). Speaker 1 is
the personnel staff member who scouts the portal. Other voices drop in and out.
Fireflies' own action-item attribution is unreliable, so the items below come
from the transcript, not its summary.

Everything below is a **request or open question**. Nothing was decided and no
workbook was changed.

Timestamps link to the recording: append `?t=<seconds>` to the URL above.

## Verdict from the room

The staff member's reaction was strongly positive. The REVIEW BOARD ordered by
projected band is what they want for pre-portal work: watch the players the data
puts at AA or AL first instead of watching by snap count. Eric's caution: validate
it internally before trusting it, and fix the missing and duplicate players first
(33:22, t=2002; 42:55, t=2575).

Target the staff member set: **30 to 50 names per position from FCS and Group of
6 schools, ready around week 5 or 6**, so they can spend the week or two before
the bye on pre-portal evals. The two-week window they named is this week and next,
before conference play (27:35, t=1655; 30:47, t=1847; 50:50, t=3050).

## Requested changes

### 1. Weekly refresh without hand pasting (priority, two-week deadline)

- Staff member asked for the easiest way to monitor this every week, and is happy
  to download and drop an Excel file each Monday or Tuesday once Telemetry updates
  (00:33, t=33; 25:14, t=1514).
- Eric's proposed design: raw Telemetry exports (likely CSV) go in a separate
  folder, Power Query loads them into PORTAL INPUT, formulas recalculate
  (24:25, t=1465).
- Cadence: weekly through the season. Useful signal needs two or three games and
  conference play, especially at lower levels (25:47, t=1547).

### 2. Pre-portal source: the Player Traits leaderboard, not the Transfer Portal

- For pre-portal, the source is the Player Traits leaderboard (FBS and FCS),
  plus Advanced Stats, not the portal view (15:13, t=913; 17:15, t=1035).
- Scope: FCS and Group of 6, "guys on the way up." Skip established Power 5
  producers (16:22, t=982).
- Staff member asked how the original portal load combined the Player Traits and
  Advanced Stats exports. Eric: there were about 30 working files behind the
  aggregate he sent (48:52, t=2932).

### 3. Leaderboard export does not match PORTAL INPUT

Tested live with a QB export (18:52 to 23:39, t=1132 to 1419):

- Extra columns (committed-to fields and others), no Elig Yrs, no jersey number.
- **Verified in the workbook today:** every REVIEW BOARD formula reads PORTAL
  INPUT by fixed position, not by header. Snaps is column H, player and QB traits
  are P:AI, advanced stats are AJ:BN, HT/WT are E/F. A paste with one column out
  of place silently corrupts every downstream flag.
- So the Drive `AGENTS.md` §6 line "column order need not match Telemetry but
  headers must" is wrong for the current formulas. The refresh (item 1) needs a
  header-to-column map.

### 4. QB trait coverage

QBs on the leaderboard have no Deep Speed and no change-of-direction or decel
values (23:17, t=1397). Effects in the current formulas:

- Speed alert still fires off Play Speed alone (it uses MAX of P and Q).
- ATHLETIC (data) uses CoD and Decel, so it goes blank for QBs. QBs can never
  reach 45 on "Critical 5 data pts".
- Elite share is unaffected in principle, since the denominator is traits graded.

### 5. Data completeness and duplicates

- Duplicate rows, for example Don Saunders listed twice (20:25, t=1225; 33:35,
  t=2015).
- Known players missing, for example DJ (11:18, t=678; 47:21, t=2841). Eric's
  guess in the room: players already rostered were never in the portal data.
  Not confirmed.
- Some Play Speed values did not come through on the export (21:28, t=1288).
- The staff member's own question: "why are there no better guys in there?"
  (33:30, t=2010).

### 6. Retrospective validation

- Run players with known grades through the bridge: the ones unanimously graded
  as legit, and the ones graded not good, and see whether the data agrees
  (07:53, t=473).
- The staff member has about 70 players already graded for the preseason Big 12
  cross-check, plus prior scout reports with AA / AL / QS / FRP grades, that could
  be the validation set (06:15, t=375; 33:45, t=2025).
- This matches the open question already in `STATUS.md`.

### 7. Size standards versus production

- Staff member wants to check whether the size standards are accurate, and asked
  whether a proven college player should get production or Player Impact in place
  of size. Example: Trayvon Mitchell, severely undersized but productive
  everywhere (34:00, t=2040).
- Eric's pushback: size caps how much production is possible, and a roster needs
  some prototypical players at each position even if most are middle of the road
  (35:35, t=2135).
- Open: swap size for Player Impact, or just cross-check Player Impact next to
  the band.

### 8. Ordering: "watch on aggregate"

- Staff member would rather watch players on aggregate than sort by one trait,
  such as accuracy alone (08:24, t=504).
- Looked for a rank column and did not find one right away. Projected band was
  there (26:35, t=1595).
- Tension with the standing rule "threshold flags, never a weighted composite."
  Note that "Critical 5 data pts" is already a summed score. Decide whether a
  sort order (band, then elite share) is enough, or whether a rank is wanted.

### 9. Explain the columns people misread

- "Critical 5 data pts (of 45)" was read in the room as five points per stat
  (29:47, t=1787). The actual formula: SUM of the five data-suggested 9/3/1
  values (SIZE, TOUGH, ATHLETIC, QUICK, SPEED) over 9 times the number of those
  factors with data. It reads "of 45" only when all five have data.
- "Adv stats elite" is the count of advanced stats at or above the 75th
  percentile. "Player Impact" is the raw Player Impact percentile.
- Add both to the README or the 007 summary.

### 10. LOW SAMPLE visibility

Asked whether LOW SAMPLE is highlighted. The text label was judged good enough
(46:38, t=2798). No change needed.

### 11. Cross-check sources outside Telemetry

PFF EPA, PFF Wins Above Average, injury reports and snap counts came up as
cross-validation for the band, not as inputs to it (38:57, t=2337; 39:27, t=2367).
The staff member has a working PFF snap-count board already (49:38, t=2978).

## Off topic

The first seven minutes covered a separate competition visit tracker whose
scraping is blocked (36 URLs) and a permission prompt on a scheduled task
(01:03 to 06:56). Not Review Board work.

# 2026-09-15 meeting: potential Review Board changes

Source: Fireflies meeting `01M2K5PNEVK662KYQ74TK2DKWD`, "Sep 15, 01:36 PM"
(untitled in Fireflies), 51 minutes.
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/view/01M2K5PNEVK662KYQ74TK2DKWD

## What kind of meeting this was

A working session, not a formal change review. Eric walked a player personnel
staff member through the 003 workbook's REVIEW BOARD. Fireflies did not name
speakers. Speaker 3 is Eric (he built the tool and sent the files). Speaker 1 is
the personnel staff member who scouts the portal. Other voices drop in and out.
Fireflies' own action-item attribution is unreliable, so the items below come
from the transcript, not its summary.

Everything below is a **request or open question**. Nothing was decided and no
workbook was changed.

Timestamps link to the recording: append `?t=<seconds>` to the URL above.

## Verdict from the room

The staff member's reaction was strongly positive. The REVIEW BOARD ordered by
projected band is what they want for pre-portal work: watch the players the data
puts at AA or AL first instead of watching by snap count. Eric's caution: validate
it internally before trusting it, and fix the missing and duplicate players first
(33:22, t=2002; 42:55, t=2575).

Target the staff member set: **30 to 50 names per position from FCS and Group of
6 schools, ready around week 5 or 6**, so they can spend the week or two before
the bye on pre-portal evals. The two-week window they named is this week and next,
before conference play (27:35, t=1655; 30:47, t=1847; 50:50, t=3050).

## Requested changes

### 1. Weekly refresh without hand pasting (priority, two-week deadline)

- Staff member asked for the easiest way to monitor this every week, and is happy
  to download and drop an Excel file each Monday or Tuesday once Telemetry updates
  (00:33, t=33; 25:14, t=1514).
- Eric's proposed design: raw Telemetry exports (likely CSV) go in a separate
  folder, Power Query loads them into PORTAL INPUT, formulas recalculate
  (24:25, t=1465).
- Cadence: weekly through the season. Useful signal needs two or three games and
  conference play, especially at lower levels (25:47, t=1547).

### 2. Pre-portal source: the Player Traits leaderboard, not the Transfer Portal

- For pre-portal, the source is the Player Traits leaderboard (FBS and FCS),
  plus Advanced Stats, not the portal view (15:13, t=913; 17:15, t=1035).
- Scope: FCS and Group of 6, "guys on the way up." Skip established Power 5
  producers (16:22, t=982).
- Staff member asked how the original portal load combined the Player Traits and
  Advanced Stats exports. Eric: there were about 30 working files behind the
  aggregate he sent (48:52, t=2932).

### 3. Leaderboard export does not match PORTAL INPUT

Tested live with a QB export (18:52 to 23:39, t=1132 to 1419):

- Extra columns (committed-to fields and others), no Elig Yrs, no jersey number.
- **Verified in the workbook today:** every REVIEW BOARD formula reads PORTAL
  INPUT by fixed position, not by header. Snaps is column H, player and QB traits
  are P:AI, advanced stats are AJ:BN, HT/WT are E/F. A paste with one column out
  of place silently corrupts every downstream flag.
- So the Drive `AGENTS.md` §6 line "column order need not match Telemetry but
  headers must" is wrong for the current formulas. The refresh (item 1) needs a
  header-to-column map.

### 4. QB trait coverage

QBs on the leaderboard have no Deep Speed and no change-of-direction or decel
values (23:17, t=1397). Effects in the current formulas:

- Speed alert still fires off Play Speed alone (it uses MAX of P and Q).
- ATHLETIC (data) uses CoD and Decel, so it goes blank for QBs. QBs can never
  reach 45 on "Critical 5 data pts".
- Elite share is unaffected in principle, since the denominator is traits graded.

### 5. Data completeness and duplicates

- Duplicate rows, for example Don Saunders listed twice (20:25, t=1225; 33:35,
  t=2015).
- Known players missing, for example DJ (11:18, t=678; 47:21, t=2841). Eric's
  guess in the room: players already rostered were never in the portal data.
  Not confirmed.
- Some Play Speed values did not come through on the export (21:28, t=1288).
- The staff member's own question: "why are there no better guys in there?"
  (33:30, t=2010).

### 6. Retrospective validation

- Run players with known grades through the bridge: the ones unanimously graded
  as legit, and the ones graded not good, and see whether the data agrees
  (07:53, t=473).
- The staff member has about 70 players already graded for the preseason Big 12
  cross-check, plus prior scout reports with AA / AL / QS / FRP grades, that could
  be the validation set (06:15, t=375; 33:45, t=2025).
- This matches the open question already in `STATUS.md`.

### 7. Size standards versus production

- Staff member wants to check whether the size standards are accurate, and asked
  whether a proven college player should get production or Player Impact in place
  of size. Example: Trayvon Mitchell, severely undersized but productive
  everywhere (34:00, t=2040).
- Eric's pushback: size caps how much production is possible, and a roster needs
  some prototypical players at each position even if most are middle of the road
  (35:35, t=2135).
- Open: swap size for Player Impact, or just cross-check Player Impact next to
  the band.

### 8. Ordering: "watch on aggregate"

- Staff member would rather watch players on aggregate than sort by one trait,
  such as accuracy alone (08:24, t=504).
- Looked for a rank column and did not find one right away. Projected band was
  there (26:35, t=1595).
- Tension with the standing rule "threshold flags, never a weighted composite."
  Note that "Critical 5 data pts" is already a summed score. Decide whether a
  sort order (band, then elite share) is enough, or whether a rank is wanted.

### 9. Explain the columns people misread

- "Critical 5 data pts (of 45)" was read in the room as five points per stat
  (29:47, t=1787). The actual formula: SUM of the five data-suggested 9/3/1
  values (SIZE, TOUGH, ATHLETIC, QUICK, SPEED) over 9 times the number of those
  factors with data. It reads "of 45" only when all five have data.
- "Adv stats elite" is the count of advanced stats at or above the 75th
  percentile. "Player Impact" is the raw Player Impact percentile.
- Add both to the README or the 007 summary.

### 10. LOW SAMPLE visibility

Asked whether LOW SAMPLE is highlighted. The text label was judged good enough
(46:38, t=2798). No change needed.

### 11. Cross-check sources outside Telemetry

PFF EPA, PFF Wins Above Average, injury reports and snap counts came up as
cross-validation for the band, not as inputs to it (38:57, t=2337; 39:27, t=2367).
The staff member has a working PFF snap-count board already (49:38, t=2978).

## Off topic

The first seven minutes covered a separate competition visit tracker whose
scraping is blocked (36 URLs) and a permission prompt on a scheduled task
(01:03 to 06:56). Not Review Board work.

I found the right project, pulled in today's Fireflies meeting, and saved the proposed Review Board changes to the repo.

**Project:** it's `PP_Recruiting`, both the repo at `DEV\PP_Recruiting` and the Drive folder `02_SPORTS\Football\PP_Recruiting`. `PlayerPersonel/` is a different project, the Jacorey Thomas film review. The "Review Board" is the REVIEW BOARD tab in `003. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx`.

**Meeting:** today's 1:36 PM recording, 51 minutes, listed in Fireflies as "Sep 15, 01:36 PM" with no real title. I read the whole transcript. It was a working session where you walked a personnel staffer through the Review Board, so the changes are things they asked for, not decisions. Fireflies didn't name speakers; from context you're Speaker 3.

**What came out of it:**
1. **Deadline:** they want a weekly refresh within two weeks, before conference play. The goal is 30 to 50 pre-portal names per position from FCS and Group of 6 schools by week 5 or 6.
2. **Data source:** for pre-portal they want to load the Player Traits leaderboard export, not the Transfer Portal export.
3. **Column mismatch:** the leaderboard export's columns don't match the paste sheet. I checked the workbook, and every Review Board formula reads the paste sheet by fixed column position, not by header name.
   - If one column is out of place, every flag is quietly wrong.
   - The Drive `AGENTS.md` says only headers need to match. That's wrong.
   - Any automated refresh needs a step that maps headers to columns.
4. **QB gaps:** QBs have no Deep Speed or change-of-direction data. The Athletic value goes blank for them, so QBs can never score 45 on "Critical 5 data pts".
5. **Data quality:** there are duplicate players (Don Saunders is listed twice) and missing ones (DJ).
6. **Validation:** they suggested checking the tool against their ~70 preseason Big 12 cross-check grades and past scout reports.
7. **Open questions:**
   - Should Player Impact replace size for undersized players who have proven themselves? You pushed back that size caps production.
   - They want to watch players "on aggregate". That conflicts with the rule against a combined score, and "Critical 5 data pts" is already a summed score.
8. **Misread column:** "Critical 5 data pts (of 45)" was read in the room as five points per stat. It's actually the five 9/3/1 values added up, out of 9 per factor that has data.

I didn't change any workbooks or add to the Drive `LOG.md`, since nothing was decided.

**Your decision:** does the weekly refresh now come before deliverable 008, the position-by-position screening matrix? I put that question at the top of Next in `STATUS.md`.

I can also rename the meeting in Fireflies to something like "PP Recruiting: Review Board walkthrough" if you want.

To merge: `gh pr create --head worktree-fireflies-review-board-0915` from the repo.

# AGENTS.md

Project: PP_Recruiting (Baylor Football Player Personnel)

## What this is

A unified grading system for Baylor Football player personnel that couples
Telemetry (Teamworks) trait percentiles with the internal S.T.A.Q.S. grading
scale, so transfer-portal data gets filtered down to the players who deserve a
scout's time. The STAQS grade stays the grade of record. Telemetry data only
decides who gets reviewed. It never produces a competing grade.

## Two locations, know which is which

Workbooks, Word deliverables and the `Send/` folder live on Google Drive:

`G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\02_SPORTS\Football\PP_Recruiting`

That folder holds the full project handoff in its own `AGENTS.md` and the
development history in `LOG.md`. Read both before doing work on the system
itself. They are the substantive spec. This repo is the version-controlled half:
documentation, decisions, and scripts.

An older copy of the project under `OneDrive - Baylor University` no longer
exists. Session logs and Codex rollouts that name that path are stale.

## Session routine

- Start: run `git pull`, then read `docs/STATUS.md` before doing anything else.
  Then read the Drive folder's `AGENTS.md` and `LOG.md`.
- End: update `docs/STATUS.md` (done, next, open questions), commit, and
  `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions

- Durable notes and decisions go in `docs/`, committed. Not in chat.
- Workbooks, documents and data exports stay on Google Drive, not in this repo.
  Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Telemetry and Teamworks are read-only. Navigate and read, never edit there.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.
- Deliverables on Drive are numbered in sequence. 007 is the latest, so the next
  one is 008.

## Standing rules carried over from the Drive handoff

- Threshold flags, never a weighted composite.
- Elite share, not raw elite count, because positions carry different trait
  counts (OL has 2, LB has 8).
- The data grades 4 of 5 critical factors, proxies Toughness, and never touches
  FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, or medical.
- Do not retry reading Telemetry's auth token or importing its internal service
  classes. Both are blocked. Scrape the rendered table instead.

# 2026-09-15 meeting: potential Review Board changes

Source: Fireflies meeting `01M2K5PNEVK662KYQ74TK2DKWD`, "Sep 15, 01:36 PM"
(untitled in Fireflies), 51 minutes.
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/view/01M2K5PNEVK662KYQ74TK2DKWD

## What kind of meeting this was

A working session, not a formal change review. Eric walked a player personnel
staff member through the 003 workbook's REVIEW BOARD. Fireflies did not name
speakers. Speaker 3 is Eric (he built the tool and sent the files). Speaker 1 is
the personnel staff member who scouts the portal. Other voices drop in and out.
Fireflies' own action-item attribution is unreliable, so the items below come
from the transcript, not its summary.

Everything below is a **request or open question**. Nothing was decided and no
workbook was changed.

Timestamps link to the recording: append `?t=<seconds>` to the URL above.

## Verdict from the room

The staff member's reaction was strongly positive. The REVIEW BOARD ordered by
projected band is what they want for pre-portal work: watch the players the data
puts at AA or AL first instead of watching by snap count. Eric's caution: validate
it internally before trusting it, and fix the missing and duplicate players first
(33:22, t=2002; 42:55, t=2575).

Target the staff member set: **30 to 50 names per position from FCS and Group of
6 schools, ready around week 5 or 6**, so they can spend the week or two before
the bye on pre-portal evals. The two-week window they named is this week and next,
before conference play (27:35, t=1655; 30:47, t=1847; 50:50, t=3050).

## Requested changes

### 1. Weekly refresh without hand pasting (priority, two-week deadline)

- Staff member asked for the easiest way to monitor this every week, and is happy
  to download and drop an Excel file each Monday or Tuesday once Telemetry updates
  (00:33, t=33; 25:14, t=1514).
- Eric's proposed design: raw Telemetry exports (likely CSV) go in a separate
  folder, Power Query loads them into PORTAL INPUT, formulas recalculate
  (24:25, t=1465).
- Cadence: weekly through the season. Useful signal needs two or three games and
  conference play, especially at lower levels (25:47, t=1547).

### 2. Pre-portal source: the Player Traits leaderboard, not the Transfer Portal

- For pre-portal, the source is the Player Traits leaderboard (FBS and FCS),
  plus Advanced Stats, not the portal view (15:13, t=913; 17:15, t=1035).
- Scope: FCS and Group of 6, "guys on the way up." Skip established Power 5
  producers (16:22, t=982).
- Staff member asked how the original portal load combined the Player Traits and
  Advanced Stats exports. Eric: there were about 30 working files behind the
  aggregate he sent (48:52, t=2932).

### 3. Leaderboard export does not match PORTAL INPUT

Tested live with a QB export (18:52 to 23:39, t=1132 to 1419):

- Extra columns (committed-to fields and others), no Elig Yrs, no jersey number.
- **Verified in the workbook today:** every REVIEW BOARD formula reads PORTAL
  INPUT by fixed position, not by header. Snaps is column H, player and QB traits
  are P:AI, advanced stats are AJ:BN, HT/WT are E/F. A paste with one column out
  of place silently corrupts every downstream flag.
- So the Drive `AGENTS.md` §6 line "column order need not match Telemetry but
  headers must" is wrong for the current formulas. The refresh (item 1) needs a
  header-to-column map.

### 4. QB trait coverage

QBs on the leaderboard have no Deep Speed and no change-of-direction or decel
values (23:17, t=1397). Effects in the current formulas:

- Speed alert still fires off Play Speed alone (it uses MAX of P and Q).
- ATHLETIC (data) uses CoD and Decel, so it goes blank for QBs. QBs can never
  reach 45 on "Critical 5 data pts".
- Elite share is unaffected in principle, since the denominator is traits graded.

### 5. Data completeness and duplicates

- Duplicate rows, for example Don Saunders listed twice (20:25, t=1225; 33:35,
  t=2015).
- Known players missing, for example DJ (11:18, t=678; 47:21, t=2841). Eric's
  guess in the room: players already rostered were never in the portal data.
  Not confirmed.
- Some Play Speed values did not come through on the export (21:28, t=1288).
- The staff member's own question: "why are there no better guys in there?"
  (33:30, t=2010).

### 6. Retrospective validation

- Run players with known grades through the bridge: the ones unanimously graded
  as legit, and the ones graded not good, and see whether the data agrees
  (07:53, t=473).
- The staff member has about 70 players already graded for the preseason Big 12
  cross-check, plus prior scout reports with AA / AL / QS / FRP grades, that could
  be the validation set (06:15, t=375; 33:45, t=2025).
- This matches the open question already in `STATUS.md`.

### 7. Size standards versus production

- Staff member wants to check whether the size standards are accurate, and asked
  whether a proven college player should get production or Player Impact in place
  of size. Example: Trayvon Mitchell, severely undersized but productive
  everywhere (34:00, t=2040).
- Eric's pushback: size caps how much production is possible, and a roster needs
  some prototypical players at each position even if most are middle of the road
  (35:35, t=2135).
- Open: swap size for Player Impact, or just cross-check Player Impact next to
  the band.

### 8. Ordering: "watch on aggregate"

- Staff member would rather watch players on aggregate than sort by one trait,
  such as accuracy alone (08:24, t=504).
- Looked for a rank column and did not find one right away. Projected band was
  there (26:35, t=1595).
- Tension with the standing rule "threshold flags, never a weighted composite."
  Note that "Critical 5 data pts" is already a summed score. Decide whether a
  sort order (band, then elite share) is enough, or whether a rank is wanted.

### 9. Explain the columns people misread

- "Critical 5 data pts (of 45)" was read in the room as five points per stat
  (29:47, t=1787). The actual formula: SUM of the five data-suggested 9/3/1
  values (SIZE, TOUGH, ATHLETIC, QUICK, SPEED) over 9 times the number of those
  factors with data. It reads "of 45" only when all five have data.
- "Adv stats elite" is the count of advanced stats at or above the 75th
  percentile. "Player Impact" is the raw Player Impact percentile.
- Add both to the README or the 007 summary.

### 10. LOW SAMPLE visibility

Asked whether LOW SAMPLE is highlighted. The text label was judged good enough
(46:38, t=2798). No change needed.

### 11. Cross-check sources outside Telemetry

PFF EPA, PFF Wins Above Average, injury reports and snap counts came up as
cross-validation for the band, not as inputs to it (38:57, t=2337; 39:27, t=2367).
The staff member has a working PFF snap-count board already (49:38, t=2978).

## Off topic

The first seven minutes covered a separate competition visit tracker whose
scraping is blocked (36 URLs) and a permission prompt on a scheduled task
(01:03 to 06:56). Not Review Board work.

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:

2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
entries.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool
entries.description: Execute JavaScript code in the context of the current page. The code runs in the page's context and can interact with the DOM, window object, and page variables. Returns the result of the last expression or any thrown errors. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. You can access and modify the DOM, call page functions, and interact with page variables.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the code in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_network_requests
entries.description: Read HTTP network requests (XHR, Fetch, documents, images, etc.) from a specific tab. Useful for debugging API calls, monitoring network activity, or understanding what requests a page is making. Returns all network requests made by the current page, including cross-origin requests. Requests are automatically cleared when the page navigates to a different domain. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to read network requests from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

urlPattern.description: Optional URL pattern to filter requests. Only requests whose URL contains this string will be returned (e.g., '/api/' to filter API calls, 'example.com' to filter by domain).

clear.description: If true, clear the network requests after reading to avoid duplicates on subsequent calls. Default is false.

limit.description: Maximum number of requests to return. Defaults to 100. Increase only if you need more results.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
entries.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__browser_batch
entries.description: Execute a sequence of browser tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — if an action navigates to a domain without permission, the next item's check fails and the batch stops. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested.

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, tabs_create_mcp). browser_batch cannot be nested.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","coordinate":[100,200],"tabId":123}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello","tabId":123}},{"name":"navigate","input":{"url":"https://example.com","tabId":123}}]

input.new_string:
## Telemetry check, same day (read-only)

Eric's browser, logged in. Looked at the Leaderboards (Player Traits and
Advanced Stats tabs) and the Transfer Portal list. Nothing edited, nothing
downloaded, no filters saved. Column lists come from each view's Manage Columns
panel, not from a downloaded file, so exact CSV header spelling is still
unconfirmed.

### Leaderboard basics

- URLs: `/ncaa/leaderboard/player-traits` and `/ncaa/leaderboard/advanced-stats`.
- Export: the "..." menu has **Download CSV** and **Download Excel**. Player
  Traits and Advanced Stats are separate tabs, so separate files. They need a
  join on player, and no player ID is visible (name, jersey, team are what show).
- Scope picker (top left, default "Power Four"): League options **FBS, FCS,
  Transfer Portal, Group of Six**, every FBS and FCS conference, every team,
  public lists (All-Americans, Senior Bowl, Combine, pre-season All-Americans)
  and Baylor's custom lists (for example "BU ROSTER 26", "Baylor Scouting
  Reports", "FALL 26' - PORTAL NEEDS"). FCS plus Group of Six is a native filter.
- Season: 2019 to 2026.
- Filter panel: Positions, States, Classes, Eligibility years left, Minimum Snaps
  (default 1).

# 2026-09-15 meeting: potential Review Board changes

Source: Fireflies meeting `01M2K5PNEVK662KYQ74TK2DKWD`, "PP Recruiting: Review
Board walkthrough" (renamed 2026-09-15 from the default "Sep 15, 01:36 PM"),
51 minutes.
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/view/01M2K5PNEVK662KYQ74TK2DKWD

## What kind of meeting this was

A working session, not a formal change review. Eric walked a player personnel
staff member through the 003 workbook's REVIEW BOARD. Fireflies did not name
speakers. Speaker 3 is Eric (he built the tool and sent the files). Speaker 1 is
the personnel staff member who scouts the portal. Other voices drop in and out.
Fireflies' own action-item attribution is unreliable, so the items below come
from the transcript, not its summary.

Everything below is a **request or open question**. Nothing was decided and no
workbook was changed.

Timestamps link to the recording: append `?t=<seconds>` to the URL above.

## Verdict from the room

The staff member's reaction was strongly positive. The REVIEW BOARD ordered by
projected band is what they want for pre-portal work: watch the players the data
puts at AA or AL first instead of watching by snap count. Eric's caution: validate
it internally before trusting it, and fix the missing and duplicate players first
(33:22, t=2002; 42:55, t=2575).

Target the staff member set: **30 to 50 names per position from FCS and Group of
6 schools, ready around week 5 or 6**, so they can spend the week or two before
the bye on pre-portal evals. The two-week window they named is this week and next,
before conference play (27:35, t=1655; 30:47, t=1847; 50:50, t=3050).

## Requested changes

### 1. Weekly refresh without hand pasting (priority, two-week deadline)

- Staff member asked for the easiest way to monitor this every week, and is happy
  to download and drop an Excel file each Monday or Tuesday once Telemetry updates
  (00:33, t=33; 25:14, t=1514).
- Eric's proposed design: raw Telemetry exports (likely CSV) go in a separate
  folder, Power Query loads them into PORTAL INPUT, formulas recalculate
  (24:25, t=1465).
- Cadence: weekly through the season. Useful signal needs two or three games and
  conference play, especially at lower levels (25:47, t=1547).

### 2. Pre-portal source: the Player Traits leaderboard, not the Transfer Portal

- For pre-portal, the source is the Player Traits leaderboard (FBS and FCS),
  plus Advanced Stats, not the portal view (15:13, t=913; 17:15, t=1035).
- Scope: FCS and Group of 6, "guys on the way up." Skip established Power 5
  producers (16:22, t=982).
- Staff member asked how the original portal load combined the Player Traits and
  Advanced Stats exports. Eric: there were about 30 working files behind the
  aggregate he sent (48:52, t=2932).

### 3. Leaderboard export does not match PORTAL INPUT

Tested live with a QB export (18:52 to 23:39, t=1132 to 1419):

- Extra columns (committed-to fields and others), no Elig Yrs, no jersey number.
- **Verified in the workbook today:** every REVIEW BOARD formula reads PORTAL
  INPUT by fixed position, not by header. Snaps is column H, player and QB traits
  are P:AI, advanced stats are AJ:BN, HT/WT are E/F. A paste with one column out
  of place silently corrupts every downstream flag.
- So the Drive `AGENTS.md` §6 line "column order need not match Telemetry but
  headers must" is wrong for the current formulas. The refresh (item 1) needs a
  header-to-column map.

### 4. QB trait coverage

QBs on the leaderboard have no Deep Speed and no change-of-direction or decel
values (23:17, t=1397). Effects in the current formulas:

- Speed alert still fires off Play Speed alone (it uses MAX of P and Q).
- ATHLETIC (data) uses CoD and Decel, so it goes blank for QBs. QBs can never
  reach 45 on "Critical 5 data pts".
- Elite share is unaffected in principle, since the denominator is traits graded.

### 5. Data completeness and duplicates

- Duplicate rows, for example Don Saunders listed twice (20:25, t=1225; 33:35,
  t=2015).
- Known players missing, for example DJ (11:18, t=678; 47:21, t=2841). Eric's
  guess in the room: players already rostered were never in the portal data.
  Not confirmed.
- Some Play Speed values did not come through on the export (21:28, t=1288).
- The staff member's own question: "why are there no better guys in there?"
  (33:30, t=2010).

### 6. Retrospective validation

- Run players with known grades through the bridge: the ones unanimously graded
  as legit, and the ones graded not good, and see whether the data agrees
  (07:53, t=473).
- The staff member has about 70 players already graded for the preseason Big 12
  cross-check, plus prior scout reports with AA / AL / QS / FRP grades, that could
  be the validation set (06:15, t=375; 33:45, t=2025).
- This matches the open question already in `STATUS.md`.

### 7. Size standards versus production

- Staff member wants to check whether the size standards are accurate, and asked
  whether a proven college player should get production or Player Impact in place
  of size. Example: Trayvon Mitchell, severely undersized but productive
  everywhere (34:00, t=2040).
- Eric's pushback: size caps how much production is possible, and a roster needs
  some prototypical players at each position even if most are middle of the road
  (35:35, t=2135).
- Open: swap size for Player Impact, or just cross-check Player Impact next to
  the band.

### 8. Ordering: "watch on aggregate"

- Staff member would rather watch players on aggregate than sort by one trait,
  such as accuracy alone (08:24, t=504).
- Looked for a rank column and did not find one right away. Projected band was
  there (26:35, t=1595).
- Tension with the standing rule "threshold flags, never a weighted composite."
  Note that "Critical 5 data pts" is already a summed score. Decide whether a
  sort order (band, then elite share) is enough, or whether a rank is wanted.

### 9. Explain the columns people misread

- "Critical 5 data pts (of 45)" was read in the room as five points per stat
  (29:47, t=1787). The actual formula: SUM of the five data-suggested 9/3/1
  values (SIZE, TOUGH, ATHLETIC, QUICK, SPEED) over 9 times the number of those
  factors with data. It reads "of 45" only when all five have data.
- "Adv stats elite" is the count of advanced stats at or above the 75th
  percentile. "Player Impact" is the raw Player Impact percentile.
- Add both to the README or the 007 summary.

### 10. LOW SAMPLE visibility

Asked whether LOW SAMPLE is highlighted. The text label was judged good enough
(46:38, t=2798). No change needed.

### 11. Cross-check sources outside Telemetry

PFF EPA, PFF Wins Above Average, injury reports and snap counts came up as
cross-validation for the band, not as inputs to it (38:57, t=2337; 39:27, t=2367).
The staff member has a working PFF snap-count board already (49:38, t=2978).

scraping is blocked (36 URLs) and a permission prompt on a scheduled task
(01:03 to 06:56). Not Review Board work.

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state

- 2026-09-14: repo created to version control the documentation and scripts for
  a project whose files live on Google Drive. No system logic changed.
- Proof of concept is complete and sitting in
  `003. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx`
  on Drive. 3,000 portal players loaded (entries on or after 1/1/2026, 100+
  snaps, FBS/FCS previous team). Results: 608 REVIEW flags, 144 of those
  uncommitted, 32 AA projections, 133 AL projections.
- Deliverables 001 through 007 are finished and on Drive. 007 is the AGM tool
  summary in Baylor style. Next deliverable number is 008.
- 2026-09-15: meeting with a player personnel staff member on the REVIEW BOARD.
  Strong buy-in, plus a list of requested changes and a two-week window. Notes
  and timestamps: `docs/2026-09-15-review-board-meeting.md`. No workbook
  changed.

## Settings currently implemented

- Elite percentile 75, poor percentile 25
- Minimum snaps 150 (LOW SAMPLE warns below this, does not suppress)

### Crosswalk check for WR / SLOT (Eric asked to re-verify)

Sources read: `000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` WR and SLOT tabs (internal eval
descriptors), and the 003 workbook's CROSSWALK and METRIC GLOSSARY tabs.

Baylor's WR and SLOT tabs use identical descriptors for all 8 factors; only the
size thresholds differ. Every factor is mapped in the CROSSWALK:

| Baylor factor (000 tab) | Elite (9) descriptor | Crosswalk primary | Crosswalk secondary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Size | Elite size | HT / WT vs SZ-SPD matrix | Power Speed |
| Toughness | Exhibits play strength / knock back | Tape only | Yards After Contact, Tackles Avoided, Tackle Breaking, Run Blocking (plus Push and Run Defense, which WRs do not carry) |
| Athletic Ability (crosswalk: Athletic Flexibility) | Fluid and balanced / bend and body control | CoD | Deceleration |
| Quickness | Rapid body movement / twitchy / explosive / sudden | Burst | Get Off (DL and LB only, not a WR metric) |
| Speed | Faster than everyone else on tape | Play Speed | Deep Speed, Adjusted Speed, Top End Speed |
| Suddenness / Route Running | Fluid / sinks in and out of breaks / separates easily | Separation | CoD, Deceleration |
| Ball Skills / Hands | Strong hands / contested catches / adjusts with ease | Ball Skills | Receiving Effectiveness |
| YAC Ability | **Explosive / Elusive / home-run threat / tough to bring down** | YAC Over Expected | Tackles Avoided, Tackle Breaking, Yards After Contact |

Findings:

- **Elusiveness is not in the crosswalk, the glossary (47 metrics), PORTAL
  INPUT, or any REVIEW BOARD formula.** The only "elusive" hits in the workbook
  are Baylor's own descriptors: WR / SLOT YAC Ability and RB Cutting Ability.
- Eric's instinct holds: the YAC Ability descriptor literally says "Elusive,"
  so Telemetry's Elusiveness belongs in that row, likely as a secondary next to
  Tackles Avoided. It is also a candidate for RB Cutting Ability.
- Probable reason it was missed: the crosswalk was built from Telemetry's
  documentation PDFs and the portal grid, and Elusiveness did not appear in
  either at the time. Not confirmed; Telemetry's own definition of Elusiveness
  still needs to be read from its Documentation pages.
- Every other WR leaderboard column has a home: Ball Skills, Tackle Breaking,
  Play Speed, Deep Speed, Burst, CoD, Decel, Run Blocking on Player Traits;
  Player Impact, Receiving Production / Effectiveness, Separation, YAC Over
  Expected, Tackles Avoided, Yards After Contact, Penalty / Penalty Drawn, Top
  End Speed, Adjusted Speed, Power Speed on Advanced Stats (Penalty is in the
  glossary as a fundamentals proxy but not on the WR crosswalk rows).
- Side effect to decide before adding it: elite share counts Player Traits
  columns only (PORTAL INPUT P:AI). Adding Elusiveness there raises the WR
  graded-trait count from 7 to 8, which shifts every WR's elite share and
  band. Putting it in Advanced Stats instead would leave elite share alone.
- Cleanup, not urgent: the Toughness and Quickness secondaries are copied
  across positions and name metrics WRs never get (Push, Run Defense, Get Off).

The WR CSV didn't download, but I finished re-checking the crosswalk, and you were right about Elusiveness.

**Crosswalk check:** I compared Baylor's WR and SLOT eval descriptors in `000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` against the 003 workbook's CROSSWALK and METRIC GLOSSARY tabs.
- **The eight WR/SLOT factors are all mapped.** WR and SLOT use identical descriptors; only the size thresholds differ.
- **Elusiveness is mapped nowhere.** It isn't in the crosswalk, the 47-metric glossary, the paste sheet or any Review Board formula. Yet Baylor's YAC Ability descriptor for WR and SLOT reads "Explosive / Elusive / Home-run threat / Tough to bring down". It currently maps to YAC Over Expected, backed by Tackles Avoided, Tackle Breaking and Yards After Contact. Elusiveness belongs there, and probably in RB Cutting Ability too.
- **Probable reason it was missed:** the crosswalk was built from Telemetry's documentation PDFs and the Transfer Portal list, and Elusiveness likely wasn't in either at the time. That's my guess, not confirmed. I haven't read Telemetry's own definition of Elusiveness yet.
- **Every other WR leaderboard column has a home** in the crosswalk or glossary.
- **Decision before adding it:** as a counted Player Trait, Elusiveness would change every WR's elite share and band. The position map says WRs have 7 traits, but the leaderboard shows 9 once Tackle Breaking and Elusiveness are included. Added as a supporting metric only, it wouldn't change elite share.
- **Minor cleanup:** the WR Toughness and Quickness rows name metrics WRs never get (Push, Run Defense, Get Off).

This is written up in the meeting note, and the Elusiveness question is in `STATUS.md` open questions. Committed and pushed on `worktree-fireflies-review-board-0915` (commit `83c25d4`).

**WR CSV download:** I set the leaderboard to WR Player Traits (Power Four, 2026) and confirmed it. # STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state

- 2026-09-14: repo created to version control the documentation and scripts for
  a project whose files live on Google Drive. No system logic changed.
- Proof of concept is complete and sitting in
  `003. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx`
  on Drive. 3,000 portal players loaded (entries on or after 1/1/2026, 100+
  snaps, FBS/FCS previous team). Results: 608 REVIEW flags, 144 of those
  uncommitted, 32 AA projections, 133 AL projections.
- Deliverables 001 through 007 are finished and on Drive. 007 is the AGM tool
  summary in Baylor style. Next deliverable number is 008.
- 2026-09-15: meeting with a player personnel staff member on the REVIEW BOARD.
  Strong buy-in, plus a list of requested changes and a two-week window. Notes
  and timestamps: `docs/2026-09-15-review-board-meeting.md`. No workbook
  changed.

## Settings currently implemented

- Elite percentile 75, poor percentile 25
- Minimum snaps 150 (LOW SAMPLE warns below this, does not suppress)
- Speed alert: Play Speed or Deep Speed at 90th percentile or higher, fires
  independently of the elite-share gate
- Review trigger: elite-trait share at or above 0.375
- Minimum graded traits to project a band: 2, else THIN

## Next

0. **Decide first:** does the weekly refresh below outrank deliverable 008?

     missing ones. See the meeting doc, items 1 to 5.
1. Deliverable 008, the one-page position-by-position screening matrix. Gap 1

2. Reconstruct `build2.py` and `load.py`. They existed only in a session

   rebuilt from code. The algorithm is written out as pseudocode in the Drive
   folder's `AGENTS.md`. See `scripts/README.md`.
3. Automate the portal pull, once the approach is approved.

## Open questions

- The 75th percentile and 0.375 share thresholds have not been validated against
  real recruiting usefulness. Eric's own note: test known prospects, including
  players the filter misses, and measure both worthwhile reviews generated and
  worthwhile players overlooked, by position.
- The Drive folder's `CLAUDE.md` has a stale file table. Its `AGENTS.md` §3 is

- From 9/15: swap size for Player Impact on proven college players, or only

  no-composite rule? Validation set: about 70 preseason Big 12 cross-check

  glossary, PORTAL INPUT and formulas, though Baylor's WR / SLOT YAC Ability
