# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state

- 2026-09-14: repo created to version control the documentation and scripts for
  a project whose files live on Google Drive. No system logic changed.
- Proof of concept is complete and sitting in
  `003. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx`
  on Drive. 3,000 portal players loaded (entries on or after 1/1/2026, 100+
  snaps, FBS/FCS previous team). Results: 608 REVIEW flags, 144 of those
  uncommitted, 32 AA projections, 133 AL projections.
- Deliverables 001 through 007 are finished and on Drive. 007 is the AGM tool
  summary in Baylor style. Next deliverable number is 008.
- 2026-09-15: meeting with a player personnel staff member on the REVIEW BOARD.
  Strong buy-in, plus a list of requested changes and a two-week window. Notes
  and timestamps: `docs/2026-09-15-review-board-meeting.md`. No workbook
  changed.

## Settings currently implemented

- Elite percentile 75, poor percentile 25
- Minimum snaps 150 (LOW SAMPLE warns below this, does not suppress)
- Speed alert: Play Speed or Deep Speed at 90th percentile or higher, fires
  independently of the elite-share gate
- Review trigger: elite-trait share at or above 0.375
- Minimum graded traits to project a band: 2, else THIN

## Next

Decided 2026-09-15 (Eric approved): 2025 baseline first, then the matrix, then
the automated weekly refresh. Reason: at week 3 the 2026 leaderboard is nearly
empty (WR CSV: Ball Skills 8 of 199, CoD and Decel 0), so a refresh built now
loads blanks, and a matrix built on unvalidated thresholds puts unproven
numbers in front of staff. The 2025 load serves both. Target: 30 to 50
pre-portal names per position by week 5 or 6.

1. **Deliverable 008: one-time 2025 leaderboard load**, FCS and Group of Six.
   - Gate: confirm 2025 FCS trait data exists. **Passed 2026-09-15** for WR
     (Leaderboards, 2025, FCS, WR Player Traits; about 900 players; 131
     sampled at four scroll depths, full-season snaps mostly 300 to 600).
     Non-blank of 130: Play Speed, Deep Speed, Burst 123; Run Blocking 105;
     Decel 70; CoD 51; Tackle Breaking 45; Elusiveness 1; Ball Skills 0. So
     FCS supports Speed, Quickness and Athletic Flexibility, while Ball Skills
     stays tape only. Other FCS position groups and Group of Six not sampled
     yet.
   - Downloads: 11 position groups x Player Traits + Advanced Stats CSVs,
     scope 2025 + FCS + Group of Six, into Drive
     `_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6/`. **2 of 22 done 2026-09-15:** WR Player
     Traits (1,101 players: 703 OWR, 398 SWR; Play Speed 1,022, Ball Skills
     356, 323 with Elig 2+) and QB Player Traits (516). Remaining: Player
     Traits RB, TE, OT, IOL, IDL, EDGE, OB-LB, SAF, CB; all 11 Advanced Stats.
   - Browser automation of Telemetry was unreliable (renderer froze, clicks
     timed out), so Eric clicks the downloads and `scripts/file_exports.py`
     names and files them by content. Traps: switching Player Traits /
     Advanced Stats tabs resets season, scope and group; the scope "Clear
     selection" button does not remove Power Four (untick the option); click
     coordinates are in the screenshot frame, not page pixels.
   - `scripts/load_leaderboard.py`: read CSVs, map headers to PORTAL INPUT,
     join Traits and Advanced Stats on `PlayerId`, write OWR / SWR as `WR` so
     POSITION MAP and SIZE STANDARDS resolve, convert Height to inches, Team
     slug into Prev Team. PlayerId, raw position code and Elusiveness go in new
     columns after Notes (BP onward) so no REVIEW BOARD formula or elite share
     changes. Keep only Elig 2 or more in 2025 data (still eligible after
     2026).
   - Write the workbook only through Excel COM, copying 003 as the template.
     openpyxl save strips the conditional formatting. Extend REVIEW BOARD
     formulas past row 3154 if the load needs more than 3,150 rows.
   - Validation run with the same script against a graded set. 000's
     `2-DEEP B12 SCOUT` tab is counts only (AA 5, AL 24, QS 105, FRP 183, LIM
     39), no names. 000's `POST-PORTAL RECAP` tab has named players with Baylor
     grades and previous team and conference (many G6): the usable seed. Also
     available: Telemetry's "Baylor Scouting Reports" custom list, and the
     staff member's ~70 preseason Big 12 cross-check grades (his file). Test the
     existing thresholds; do not tune them in the same pass.
   - Append Drive `LOG.md` when 008 is created.
   - Loader written and tested 2026-09-15 on the 2026 Power Four WR Player
     Traits CSV, built into a scratch copy (not Drive): 199 rows, OWR / SWR
     resolved to WR, no unmapped headers, formulas recalculated with no errors,
     conditional formatting counts identical to 003 (2 and 13), old portal rows
     cleared. See `scripts/README.md`.
   - Watch in validation, do not fix mid-test: SETTINGS SIZE STANDARDS has one
     WR row (74 in for a 9) and no SLOT row, so slot receivers get WR size
     values. In the test build 91 of 199 WRs scored SIZE 1.
2. **Deliverable 009: the screening matrix** (was 008), drafted from what the
   validation run shows. See `docs/open-work.md`.
3. **Weekly refresh**, automated once 2026 data fills in (weeks 5 to 6). The
   staff member runs it himself, so it may belong in Power Query inside the
   workbook rather than Python. Decide then.
2. Reconstruct `build2.py` and `load.py`. They existed only in a session
   container and are gone, so the 002 and 003 workbooks cannot currently be
   rebuilt from code. The algorithm is written out as pseudocode in the Drive
   folder's `AGENTS.md`. See `scripts/README.md`.
3. Automate the portal pull, once the approach is approved.

## Open questions

- The 75th percentile and 0.375 share thresholds have not been validated against
  real recruiting usefulness. Eric's own note: test known prospects, including
  players the filter misses, and measure both worthwhile reviews generated and
  worthwhile players overlooked, by position.
- The Drive folder's `CLAUDE.md` has a stale file table. Its `AGENTS.md` §3 is
  the current list. Decide whether to fix or retire that file.
- From 9/15: swap size for Player Impact on proven college players, or only
  cross-check it? Is sorting by band enough, or is a rank wanted, given the
  no-composite rule? Validation set: about 70 preseason Big 12 cross-check
  grades plus prior scout reports.
- Elusiveness (Telemetry WR Player Trait) is missing from the CROSSWALK,
  glossary, PORTAL INPUT and formulas, though Baylor's WR / SLOT YAC Ability
  descriptor says "Elusive." Add it to YAC Ability (and RB Cutting Ability)?
  As a counted Player Trait it would change WR elite share (POSITION MAP says
  7 WR traits; the leaderboard shows 9); as a secondary / Advanced-side metric
  it would not. Verified 2026-09-15.

## Gotchas

- REVIEW BOARD formulas read PORTAL INPUT by fixed column position (H, P:AI,
  AJ:BN, E/F), not by header. Verified 2026-09-15. The Drive `AGENTS.md` §6
  claim that only headers must match is wrong. Any import has to land columns
  in the exact 67-column order.
- Leaderboard exports are not portal exports (checked 2026-09-15): WRs come as
  OWR/SWR (POSITION MAP only knows WR), Height is "6-4" text, Top End Speed is on
  the Advanced Stats tab, QB views have no Deep Speed or Decel column, Traits and
  Advanced Stats are separate files joined on the CSV's `PlayerId` column, and
  Team comes as a slug (`southern-california`). At week 3 the WR CSV had almost
  no trait values (Ball Skills 8 of 199, CoD and Decel 0). Full map in
  `docs/2026-09-15-review-board-meeting.md`.

- Telemetry's calendar arrows move two months at a time, and the end date cannot
  exceed Telemetry's own "today".
- "Apply Filters" sometimes needs a second click. Check the "Filter (n)" count.
- If the pager shows Next disabled on page 1, reload. Filters survive a reload,
  window state does not, so export scraped data before reloading.
- The portal table is virtualized, roughly 20 rows in the DOM at 100 rows per
  page. Scroll the container, then click Next page by aria-label.

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state

- 2026-09-14: repo created to version control the documentation and scripts for
  a project whose files live on Google Drive. No system logic changed.
- Proof of concept is complete and sitting in
  `003. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx`
  on Drive. 3,000 portal players loaded (entries on or after 1/1/2026, 100+
  snaps, FBS/FCS previous team). Results: 608 REVIEW flags, 144 of those
  uncommitted, 32 AA projections, 133 AL projections.
- Deliverables 001 through 007 are finished and on Drive. 007 is the AGM tool
  summary in Baylor style. Next deliverable number is 008.
- 2026-09-15: meeting with a player personnel staff member on the REVIEW BOARD.
  Strong buy-in, plus a list of requested changes and a two-week window. Notes
  and timestamps: `docs/2026-09-15-review-board-meeting.md`. No workbook
  changed.

## Settings currently implemented

- Elite percentile 75, poor percentile 25
- Minimum snaps 150 (LOW SAMPLE warns below this, does not suppress)
- Speed alert: Play Speed or Deep Speed at 90th percentile or higher, fires
  independently of the elite-share gate
- Review trigger: elite-trait share at or above 0.375
- Minimum graded traits to project a band: 2, else THIN

## Next

Decided 2026-09-15 (Eric approved): 2025 baseline first, then the matrix, then
the automated weekly refresh. Reason: at week 3 the 2026 leaderboard is nearly
empty (WR CSV: Ball Skills 8 of 199, CoD and Decel 0), so a refresh built now
loads blanks, and a matrix built on unvalidated thresholds puts unproven
numbers in front of staff. The 2025 load serves both. Target: 30 to 50
pre-portal names per position by week 5 or 6.

1. **Deliverable 008: one-time 2025 leaderboard load**, FCS and Group of Six.
   - Gate: confirm 2025 FCS trait data exists. **Passed 2026-09-15** for WR
     (Leaderboards, 2025, FCS, WR Player Traits; about 900 players; 131
     sampled at four scroll depths, full-season snaps mostly 300 to 600).
     Non-blank of 130: Play Speed, Deep Speed, Burst 123; Run Blocking 105;
     Decel 70; CoD 51; Tackle Breaking 45; Elusiveness 1; Ball Skills 0. So
     FCS supports Speed, Quickness and Athletic Flexibility, while Ball Skills
     stays tape only. Other FCS position groups and Group of Six not sampled
     yet.
   - **Done 2026-09-15.** 22 of 22 CSVs (scope 2025 + FCS + Group of Six) in
     Drive `_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6/`; 14,068 unique players.
     **`008. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (2025 FCS-G6
     BASELINE).xlsx` is on Drive**: 5,560 players with Elig 2+, verified in
     Excel (formulas through row 5564, zero errors, formatting intact). 441
     REVIEW flags: QB 23, RB 46, WR 58, TE 23, OT 24, OG 23, C 9, IDL 43,
     EDGE 50, OB-LB 32, CB 63, SAF 47. Bands AA 24, AL 82, QS 312, FRP 649,

# scripts

## load_leaderboard.py

Loads Telemetry **leaderboard** CSV exports (Leaderboards > Player Traits or
Advanced Stats > "..." > Download CSV) into a new numbered grading workbook. It
is the data-load half of the lost `load.py`, rebuilt for leaderboard exports.

```
uv run --with openpyxl --with pywin32 python scripts/load_leaderboard.py ^
    --csv-dir "<folder of downloaded CSVs>" ^
    --template "<Drive>\003. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx" ^
    --stage-dir "<scratch folder>" ^
    --min-elig 2 ^
    --out "<Drive>\008. <name>.xlsx"
```

Omit `--out` to stage only (no Excel): writes `portal_input_stage.csv` and
`load_report.json` to `--stage-dir`.

What it does:

- Reads PORTAL INPUT row 4 headers from the template, so the column order always
  matches the formulas (they read by fixed position, not header).
- Joins Player Traits and Advanced Stats rows on the CSV's `PlayerId`.
- Maps header names that differ (`Pos.`, `Elig.`, `Weight`, `Team`, throw
  velocities, Top End Speed). Converts Height `6-2` to inches. Folds State into
  Hometown. Team slug goes into Prev Team.
- Maps leaderboard position codes to POSITION MAP codes (OWR and SWR to WR, and
  the POSITION MAP aliases). The raw code is kept.
- `--min-elig 2` keeps players still eligible after the season in the data. Use
  it for a 2025 pre-portal pull.
- PlayerId, raw position, Elusiveness and source file go in columns after Notes.
  Columns A:BO keep their meaning, so REVIEW BOARD, traits graded and elite share
  are unchanged.
- Builds the workbook through **Excel COM**, never openpyxl save (that strips the
  conditional formatting). Refuses to overwrite an existing file. Extends
  PORTAL INPUT and REVIEW BOARD rows past the template's last row when needed.

Check `load_report.json` after every run: `unmapped_csv_headers` and
`unknown_position_codes` must be empty or explained before using the workbook.

Data stays on Drive or in a scratch folder. Never commit CSVs, stage files or
workbooks here.

## file_exports.py

Files Telemetry leaderboard downloads from the Downloads folder into a Drive
export folder with consistent names, identifying each file by content (Chrome
often leaves them as `<uuid>.tmp`).

```
uv run python scripts/file_exports.py --downloads "C:/Users/eric_rash/Downloads" ^
    --dest "<Drive>/PP_Recruiting/_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6" ^
    --prefix 2025_fcs-g6 --since "2026-09-15 16:00" [--dry-run]
```

- Tab from the header (`Player Impact` present = Advanced Stats), group from the
  `Pos.` codes (OWR/SWR to WR, OG/C to IOL).
- Names files `<prefix>_<GROUP>_<player-traits|advanced-stats>.csv`.
- Copies, verifies byte for byte, then deletes the download. Never overwrites;
  duplicates and unclear files are reported and left in Downloads.
- Run with `--dry-run` first.

Loads Telemetry **leaderboard** CSV exports (Leaderboards > Player Traits or
Advanced Stats > "..." > Download CSV) into a new numbered grading workbook. It

    --csv-dir "<folder of downloaded CSVs>" ^
    --template "<Drive>\003. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx" ^

`load_report.json` to `--stage-dir`.

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what>
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.
```

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\memory-write

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

entries.name: ExitWorktree
entries.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree
